Rasters as height surfaces

Source: R/stats-raster.R
geom_spatraster_3d.Rd

Draws each layer of a terra SpatRaster or a stars object as a surface whose height and fill are the cell values. Cells are the grid nodes at their centres; missing cells leave holes. Rasters with more than maxcell cells are first resampled to a regular sample of about maxcell cells, as tidyterra's geom_spatraster() does. Layers (or bands) are separate surfaces grouped by the computed lyr variable, ready for facet_wrap(~lyr).

Usage

geom_spatraster_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  maxcell = 50000,
  shade = TRUE,
  wireframe = FALSE,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = FALSE
)

Arguments

mapping, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

data

A terra SpatRaster or a stars object.

maxcell

Largest number of cells drawn per layer.

shade

Whether to apply lighting.

wireframe

Whether to draw triangle edges.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

The computed variables are value (the mean cell value of each triangle, the default fill), lyr, and z_mean. A geographic raster needs a projected target, coord_3d(crs = ); the cells keep their lattice when reprojected.

fortify() methods turn SpatRaster and stars objects into data frames with x, y, value and lyr columns at full resolution, and lidR LAS point clouds into one row per point with x, y, z, intensity, classification and the other point attributes in snake case.

See also

stat_profile_3d() for cross-sections through the surface.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  r <- terra::rast(volcano[nrow(volcano):1, ], extent = terra::ext(0, 610, 0, 870))
  ggplot2::ggplot() + geom_spatraster_3d(data = r, maxcell = 2000) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c() + coord_3d(aspect = c(610, 870, 300))
}
if (requireNamespace("stars", quietly = TRUE)) {
  s <- stars::st_as_stars(volcano)
  ggplot2::ggplot() + geom_spatraster_3d(data = s, maxcell = 1500) + coord_3d()
}
if (requireNamespace("lidR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  las <- lidR::readLAS(system.file("extdata", "MixedConifer.laz", package = "lidR"),
    filter = "-keep_random_fraction 0.05")
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::fortify(las), ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, colour = z)) +
    geom_point_3d(size = 0.3) + coord_3d(aspect = c(1, 1, 0.4))
}
